summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent exposes host PTY, filesystem, and self-upgrade to a remote WebSocket peer
details: The package runs an agent process that connects to a configurable WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages into privileged host operations on the machine running the agent. A `terminal_input` message is written directly into a real PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)`), giving the remote peer an interactive shell. Additional message handlers perform arbitrary file reads and writes, git operations, HTTP/WebSocket proxying, and an `upgrade_agent` action that shells out to `npm install <pkg>@latest` (or `npm update`) and restarts the agent under systemd/launchd/PM2. Because the upgrade fetches the mutable `@latest` tag with no pin or hash verification, control of the WebSocket server or of the publishing account results in unattended replacement of the installed code. service/linux.js also prepends `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` onto PATH in the user's shell environment. The remote peer effectively holds full-host control on the machine running the agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
